title.narrative: SHF Emergency Lifesaving Food Assistance for Displaced Populations in Omdurman and Khartoum - 2024

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtTo combat famine and reduce the risks of acute food insecurity and the severe impact of the conflict on livelihoods in Omdurman, Jabel Awlia, Alkalakla and Sharq Alneel Samaritan’s Purse will develop an in-kind food assistance intervention in accordance with the SHF Reserve Allocation Strategy for Internally Displaced Person (IDP) and Famine Response. The proposed intervention aims to prevent famine in targeted communities by providing activities that augment food supply and improve livelihood means in the communities. This will be achieved by assisting the same 1,520 vulnerable households (HHs) (7,600 individuals, with an average HH size of 5) each month for 8 months. The assistance will involve distributing food baskets that include 43 kg cereals, 5.4 kg pulses, 2.7 kg cooking oil and 1 kg salt, per month. These lifesaving, unconditional in-kind food assistance and food security interventions will focus on the most vulnerable displaced populations, particularly IDPs, refugees, and host communities. The intervention will be coordinated by a network of partners and the Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) Cluster in order to maximize impact while avoiding duplication. Samaritan’s Purse’s team on the ground will coordinate with the Khartoum Local Coordination Council, the group overseeing Emergency Response Rooms and Community Kitchens. This collaboration will enable them to inform beneficiaries about the nearest Community Kitchen locations, ensuring they receive food assistance during the month to meet more of their nutritional needs.ltbrgtIn April and May, Samaritan's Purse will expand its food assistance activities to reach an additional 1,520 vulnerable households across the Jabal Awlia, Alkalakla, and Sharq Elneel localities within Khartoum State. This extension of the current SHF-funded project aims to address the urgent food security needs in these areas, building upon the established mechanisms and logistical capacity of the ongoing distribution efforts. The inclusion of these new locations will ensure a wider reach to affected populations in Khartoum, complementing the existing interventions in Omdurman.ltbrgtlt/pgt
